title: Mainaka
hook: halfway across the sea, a golden mountain rises out of the water and offers Hanuman a place to rest
carry: your welcome is as good as done

segments.voice: Yesterday: the long flight, trees falling like family at the gate, and a shadow sailing on the sea.

You're driving a long way, late, and a friend texts: you're passing my town, come in, I've made dinner, sleep here. It's a real kindness. But if you stop, you won't get where you're going in time. That's the first test Hanuman meets over the ocean, and it isn't a monster. It's a gift. The sea has been watching him, and the sea feels it owes him something.
screen: `COME IN, I'VE MADE DINNER.` → `THE FIRST TEST IS A GIFT.`

segments.voice: In Valmiki's telling, the Ocean is a person who thinks and remembers, and it remembers a debt. Long ago King Sagara, an ancestor of Rama's own line, had sons who dug out the bed of the sea; tradition says that's why the ocean is called sagara. So the Ocean thinks: this monkey is on an errand for Rama, of the family that made me what I am. He shouldn't wear himself out. It calls to a mountain hidden beneath its waves, Mainaka, to rise and give the traveler a place to rest. Mainaka lifts out of the water, golden peaks shining, trees on his slopes, takes a human form on the summit, and invites Hanuman to rest, eat fruit, and then go on. Hanuman's first reaction is suspicion: a mountain rising in his path looks like an obstacle, and he pushes it aside with his chest. Then Mainaka explains, and Hanuman understands. He answers with great courtesy. I'm grateful. Your welcome is as good as done. But time is pressing, and I've promised not to stop on the way. He touches the mountain with his hand, honoring the offer, and flies on. Refusing a threat is easy to understand. Refusing kindness without hurting the one who offers it takes skill. Hanuman doesn't lecture, and he doesn't rest a little to be polite. He receives the gift by touching it, and keeps his promise.
screen: `THE OCEAN REMEMBERS A DEBT.` · `MAINAKA RISES TO OFFER REST.` · `TIME PRESSES; I'VE PROMISED.` · then, large: `HE TOUCHES THE MOUNTAIN AND GOES ON.`

segments.voice: Rest one hand lightly on your knee, the way Hanuman's hand touches the mountain, and think of an offer you'll probably have to turn down soon. Breathe in and feel genuinely grateful for it; breathe out and keep your direction. Let the hand stay light, honoring without holding.
Mainaka. The golden mountain under the sea who rises at the Ocean's request to offer Hanuman rest, and whom Hanuman thanks with a touch before flying on.
Your line: your welcome is as good as done. Mainaka has a reason of his own, too. That's day six hundred six.

howItsDone: In Sundara Kanda recitations, Mainaka is remembered as the first of three meetings over the sea, and Hanuman's touch of the mountain is often explained as accepting the hospitality without stopping.

trapdoor: what you thought: Hanuman's tests over the sea are all monsters.
what it means: the first one is a gift, and the test is declining it gracefully.
what a scholar hears: the Ocean's gratitude ties this scene to the Bala Kanda story of King Sagara's sons, linking Hanuman's crossing to Rama's ancestry.

chat.says: If the mountain offered Hanuman food and rest, why didn't he stop?
options: He'd promised not to stop, so he thanked Mainaka with a touch and flew on.
He thought Mainaka was a trap and pushed past without a word.
He wasn't tired at all, so a rest would have been rude to accept.
chat.meaning: Time was pressing and he'd promised not to stop, so he honored the kindness with a touch of his hand and kept going.

Mainaka.meaning: a golden mountain under the sea that rises to offer rest

Sagara.meaning: an ancient king of Rama's line whose sons dug the sea

Valmiki.meaning: the poet-sage traditionally credited with the Ramayana

Rama.meaning: the exiled prince whose wife Sita was taken

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda 1 (the Ocean's request; Mainaka rises; Hanuman declines)
Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 38–44 (King Sagara and his sons)

notes: The Ocean's reasoning (debt to the Ikshvaku line through Sagara's sons) and Mainaka's human form on the summit: confirm against Sundara 1.
Hanuman first pushes Mainaka aside with his chest as an obstacle, then understands: confirm.
Bala Kanda sarga range for the Sagara story: confirm.
The explanation of the name sagara for the ocean is traditional; confirm the Keeper is comfortable with it.
